_meta.title: 英文十四行诗阅读与修改建议 Reading English Sonnets and Revision Suggestions
_meta.description:
本问卷邀请您阅读三首英文十四行诗并给出三维修改建议。预计15-25分钟。请用骰子或手机秒数随机选择分支A/B/C。
Read three English sonnets and give revision suggestions on three dimensions. 15-25 min. Use a die or phone-seconds digit to pick branch A/B/C.

title:
【研究说明 Study Information】
您好!诚邀参与诗歌审美判断与修改建议研究。参与自愿,可随时退出。
Hello! You are invited to a study on poetic aesthetic judgment and revision suggestions. Participation is voluntary; you may stop anytime.
回答仅用于学术研究;不作个人身份公开披露。Responses are for academic research only.
部分诗歌可能由模型生成;作答期间不告知生成细节。Some poems may be model-generated; details withheld during the survey.

我已阅读以上说明,并同意参与本研究。
I have read the information above and agree to participate.
options: 同意,继续作答 / Agree - continue
不同意,退出问卷 / Do not agree - exit

title:
您如何描述自己在诗歌(阅读或写作)方面的经验?
How would you describe your experience with poetry (reading or writing)?
options: 业余/日常读者 - Amateur / casual reader
有一定基础 - Intermediate (coursework or regular reading)
较专业 - Expert (advanced study, publication, teaching, or practice)

title:
您对英文格律诗(音步、押韵等)进行评判的自信程度?
Rate your confidence evaluating English formal verse (meter/rhyme).
1=完全不自信 not at all confident; 7=非常自信 highly confident

您进行文学阅读时最常用的主要语言是?(例如:中文、英文)
What is your primary language for literary reading? (e.g., Chinese, English)

您是否学习或系统阅读过莎士比亚体十四行诗(Shakespearean sonnet: 14行, 韵式 ABAB CDCD EFEF GG)?
Have you studied Shakespearean sonnets?

【评判说明 Guidelines】请写具体、可执行的修改指令,避免空泛评价。
Please write specific, actionable revision instructions; avoid vague comments.
1) Tension 张力: 冲突/对照/未解决张力。 Conflict/contrast/unresolved force.
2) Symbol(Imagery) 象征意象: 感官意象与象征。 Concrete imagery and symbols.
3) Rhythm 节奏韵律: 行节奏与韵式 ABAB CDCD EFEF GG。 Cadence and rhyme scheme.
诗歌正文为英文;建议可用中文或英文。 Poems in English; suggestions may be CN/EN.

【如何随机选择分支 How to choose your branch】
本平台无法自动随机分配。请用相对客观的随机方式决定分支。
This platform cannot auto-assign. Use an objective random method.
方式1 掷六面骰: 1或2=A; 3或4=B; 5或6=C。
Method 1 die: 1-2=A; 3-4=B; 5-6=C.
方式2 手机秒数个位: 1-2或7-8=A; 3-4或9/0=B; 5-6=C。
Method 2 seconds digit: 1-2 or 7-8=A; 3-4 or 9/0=B; 5-6=C.
请先随机,再答下面两题。勿按喜好挑选。 Draw first, then answer the next two items. Do not choose by preference.

您用于决定分支的随机结果是?(骰子点数或秒数个位)
What random outcome did you get? (die face or seconds digit)

请根据上一题随机结果选择问卷分支(1-2或7-8=A; 3-4或9/0=B; 5-6=C)。
Select your branch from the random outcome (1-2 or 7-8=A; 3-4 or 9/0=B; 5-6=C).

【分支A Branch A】诗歌1 / Poem 1
(staff id: gen0_t1a)
请完整阅读下列英文十四行诗,然后回答随后三题。
Please read the English sonnet below in full, then answer the next three items.
---- poem begin ----
The year's last roses lean to touch the pane,
And swallows stitch the dusk in fading flight;
The orchard's gold is thinned by coming rain,
And hills are folded in the failing light.
A shutter taps where vines have overgrown,
The garden bench is cold, the paths are bare;
The asters bow their heads on stalks alone,
And silence settles in the waiting air.
No more the urgent hum of summer's trade,
No more the long, warm hours that used to be;
The season's promise slowly is unmade,
And what was green is now a memory.
So let the leaves fall quiet, one by one-
The year departs, and so does all begun.
---- poem end ----

---- poem begin ----
The city sheds its clamor, street by street,
And leaves a hush where engines used to churn.
The pavement holds the memory of feet,
While lonely window-lights begin to burn.
A single figure, cloaked in amber glow,
Moves past the shuttered shops and silent cars,
Whose metal bodies, parked in even row,
Reflect the faded glory of the stars.
The air is thin, a breath of stone and steel,
That cools the fevered pulse of hurried days.
No voice returns the thoughts that turn and wheel,
Lost in the labyrinth of empty ways.
So solitude becomes a quiet friend,
Who walks beside me to the journey's end.
---- poem end ----

Please read the English sonnet below in full, then answer the next three items.
---- poem begin ----
The river keeps what daylight cannot hold-
A glint of oar, a whisper on the stone-
And in its deep, where quiet currents fold,
I find the face I thought I had outgrown.
The rain that fell on some forgotten June
Still taps its code along the window ledge,
A pulse that slows beneath a listless moon,
A name I trace along the water's edge.
What drifts is not the loss but what remains-
The cool, wet gravity of that first glance,
The way a ripple loosens all my chains,
And lets the drowned light surface, slow, by chance.
So let the stream unspool its silver thread-
I drink the past, and it has gone to bed.
---- poem end ----

---- poem begin ----
The amber leaves, reluctant, quit the bough,
And drift in spirals on the dying air;
The sun, a ghost, grows paler even now,
And shadows stretch like fingers of despair.
The robin's song, once rich with summer's fire,
Is thinned to whispers in the bramble's gray;
The fields that blazed with gold and green retire
To stubble where the lonely ploughshare may.
But hark! Not all is silence-far above,
A wedge of wild geese cleaves the ashen sky,
Their cries a brazen testament of love
That will not let the fading season die.
So though the world undresses into night,
Their southward flight becomes my stubborn light.
---- poem end ----

---- poem begin ----
The city breathes in iron lung at night,
And windows gleam like eyes that do not sleep;
The asphalt rivers hold the lonely light,
Where shadows crawl and tangled sorrows creep.
I walk a canyon made of stone and steel,
My footsteps echo where no footstep stays,
A pulse I feel but never can reveal,
Lost in the maze of these electric days.
But then-a sudden flare, a taxi's brake!
The world lurches and shatters my still trance;
A drunkard's laugh, a siren's wail awake
The ghost of motion in this vast expanse.
Yet no hand reaches, no voice calls my name-
I am the echo, and the echo's shame.
---- poem end ----

Please read the English sonnet below in full, then answer the next three items.
---- poem begin ----
The mind is not a vessel, but a tide
That turns upon a shore of vanished years;
It coils the kelp of moments, set aside
In briny hollows, salt with unshed tears.
The drowned town's bell still tolls beneath the deep,
A muffled chime the current bends and braids;
The faces that we loved in silence sleep
Where coral builds her patient, cold arcades.
But wake!-this flood is not a grave, but glass
That shatters on the keel of a new sun!
What once was drowned, the living waves surpass-
The sea that took, the sea returns as one.
So let the brine recast what time unwove:
The tide that lost you is the tide I love.
---- poem end ----
